item.description: Humidity can rapidly alter hybrid-perovskite surfaces, yet the earliest topographic processes linking water adsorption to chemical degradation remain poorly resolved. Here, we tracked the same air-cleaved methylammonium lead bromide (MAPbBr(3)) single-crystal surface using consecutive non-contact atomic force microscopy measurements during a controlled increase in relative humidity (RH). The initial surface contained atomically flat terraces, single-unit-cell steps, and pre-existing PbBr(x)...

item.title: Associations Between Hospice Care Duties and Compassion Fatigue Among Nurses in Korea: The Roles of End-of-Life Care Stress and Peer Support
item.description: CONCLUSION: Perceived duty difficulty showed a cross-sectional indirect association with compassion fatigue through EOLCS, while its conditional association varied across peer support levels. These findings highlight the relevance of considering perceived duty difficulty together with EOLCS and peer support when examining compassion fatigue among hospice nurses.

item.title: Cytokine profiles of aqueous humor from sequential bilateral cataract surgery: Impact of diabetes on inflammatory responses
item.description: We investigated aqueous humor (AH) cytokine profiles in first- and second-operated eyes of patients undergoing sequential bilateral cataract surgery and explored these profiles according to diabetes mellitus (DM) status. This retrospective, within-subject, comparative observational study included 71 patients, comprising 39 without DM and 32 with DM but without diabetic retinopathy, who underwent uneventful sequential bilateral cataract surgery within a 2-week interval. The concentrations of...

item.title: Baseline Physical Frailty Predicts Clinical Outcomes During Lecanemab Therapy in Early Alzheimer's Disease: A Prospective Real-World Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Baseline SPPB-defined physical frailty was associated with longitudinal clinical progression and IRRs during lecanemab treatment. These findings suggest that SPPB-defined physical frailty may represent a candidate prognostic marker of clinical outcomes during lecanemab therapy and warrant further validation in larger cohorts.

item.title: Olfactory Receptor 51E2 Activation by β-Ionone Induces a Senescence-Like Phenotype and Increases Susceptibility to Senolytic Treatment in Colorectal Cancer
item.description: Olfactory receptor 51E2 (OR51E2) is markedly downregulated in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet its functional activation by its natural agonist, β-ionone, suppresses CRC cell growth. In this study, we investigated the tumor-suppressive effects of β-ionone-mediated OR51E2 activation using human CRC cell lines (SW480, SW620, and RKO) and patient-derived organoids (PDOs). We demonstrate that β-ionone treatment stimulates intracellular calcium levels in an OR51E2-dependent manner, upregulating...

item.title: Simplifying CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 Maintains Diagnostic Performance: An Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Simplifying LI-RADS v2018 by removing TG and using a 10-mm size cut-off preserved diagnostic table AUC while improving LR-5 sensitivity without loss of specificity or PPV.

item.title: Efficacy and Safety of Evogliptin in Mild to Moderate Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis: The EVOID-AS Trial Rationale and Study Design
item.description: The only treatment of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is aortic valve replacement. No medical therapy has been proven effective for preventing or delaying AS progression despite several clinical trials. The EVOID-AS trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy of evogliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor, at retarding the progression of aortic valve calcification and AS hemodynamic severity in patients with mild to moderate AS. In this trial, 580 patients with mild or moderate native calcific AS...

item.title: AxialTAD: an axial contrast architecture for TAD boundary prediction from Hi-C
item.description: Topologically associating domains (TADs) are fundamental units of 3D chromatin organization, and accurate identification of TAD boundaries from Hi-C contact matrices remains an active challenge. Recent deep learning approaches have advanced substantially, but these rely on increasingly large architectures, raising the question of how much of this capacity boundary-centric analysis requires. Here we propose AxialTAD, a compact deep learning model centered on an Axial Contrast Module (ACM) that...

item.title: Pressure Injury Risk Factors in Hospice and Palliative Care: Integrating End-of-Life Symptoms Into Nursing Assessment
item.description: Pressure injuries are common complications among patients with terminal cancer receiving inpatient hospice care, and the physiological changes that occur at the end of life may not be fully reflected in conventional risk assessment. This retrospective cross-sectional study examined factors associated with pressure injuries at admission among 1158 patients with terminal cancer admitted to an inpatient hospice and palliative care unit in South Korea, of who 386 (33.3%) had pressure injuries at...

item.title: Development and Evaluation of WELSH: An Institution-Linked Mobile Application for Older Adults in Senior Welfare Centers During COVID-19
item.description: BackgroundCOVID-19 closures of South Korean senior welfare centers isolated older adults. We developed and evaluated "WELSH," an age-friendly, institution-linked mobile app, using the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) framework.MethodsFollowing needs assessments, WELSH was implemented across five Seoul centers. During a 2-week pilot, 376 older adults completed pre- and post-intervention questionnaires evaluating usability, digital literacy, and psychosocial...

item.title: Comparative genomics reveals expanded cell-surface signaling and siderophore scavenging repertoires in Pectobacterium
item.description: Iron acquisition in gram-negative bacteria relies on TonB-dependent receptors (TBDRs), some of which initiate cell-surface signaling (CSS) by activating extracytoplasmic function (ECF) sigma factors that induce cognate transport pathways. Although well characterized in Pseudomonas, CSS systems remain poorly explored in plant-associated bacteria. Surveying 6,847 plant-associated bacterial genomes revealed near-ubiquitous CSS systems in Pseudomonas and Pectobacterium, with markedly lower...

item.title: Avoidable mortality among temperature-attributable deaths in South Korea, 1990-2023
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although temperature-related risks and attributable fractions were higher for non-avoidable mortality, nearly one-third of temperature-attributable deaths occurred in the avoidable category. While limiting exposure to non-optimum temperatures remains the principal strategy for alleviating this burden, preventive care and disease management may provide a complementary approach.
item.category: Korea University, Pusan National University, SNU

item.title: Clinical and behavioral delineation of cochlear implant non-users: a 20-year retrospective descriptive analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND SIGNIFICANCE: CI non-use is driven by distinct physiological, psychological, and socioeconomic factors depending on deafness onset. Delineating these onset-specific profiles provides essential guidance for tailored preoperative counseling and age-appropriate post-implantation monitoring to minimize long-term device abandonment.

item.title: Conductivity-To-Tissue Volume Ratio: Imaging Biomarker for the Alzheimer's Disease Continuum
item.description: While hippocampal volume and tissue conductivity are independent markers of neurodegeneration, their integrated diagnostic utility in Alzheimer's disease remains underexplored. This prospective cross-sectional study evaluated a novel conductivity-to-tissue volume ratio index across the Alzheimer's disease continuum. Overall, 110 participants-30 cognitively normal adults, 52 with amnestic mild cognitive impairment, and 28 with Alzheimer's disease-underwent magnetic resonance electrical properties...

item.title: Bias Polarity Switching (BiPS): A Transient Method for Probing Interfacial Carrier Dynamics
item.description: Interfaces and contacts critically influence the performance and stability of semiconductor devices, yet direct experimental access to charge accumulation and release processes near biased interfaces remains limited. Here, we introduce the Bias Polarity Switching (BiPS) technique as a transient method for probing carrier dynamics in the sub-/micrometer-scale near-interface region under realistic operating conditions. We show that BiPS enables distinction between free- and trapped-carrier...

item.title: Micro-3D-printed integrated system with liquid-metal coils for simultaneous size-selective sampling and concentration sensing of respirable ferrous metal aerosols
item.description: Respirable ferrous metal aerosols generated during metal processing and transportation pose exposure risks, motivating compact systems that can simultaneously classify particles by size and assess ferrous-particle concentrations. Conventional inductive sensors typically employ relatively large wire-wound coils and sensing channels, limiting their responses to few-micrometer particles. Here, we present a micro-3D-printed sampling-to-sensing platform integrating a two-stage inertial impactor,...

item.title: Correction: Geometry driven machine learning guided fabrication of sub-5 µm PLGA microparticles for balloon catheter drug delivery
item.description: Correction for 'Geometry driven machine learning guided fabrication of sub-5 µm PLGA microparticles for balloon catheter drug delivery' by Mohamed S. Ibrahim et al., Anal. Methods, 2026, 18, 7945-7958, https://doi.org/10.1039/d6ay00884d.

item.title: Optimal Exercise Dose for Improving Multidimensional Health Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer Patients: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression
item.description: This study aimed to investigate the dose-response relationships between exercise prescription parameters and a range of health outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). The following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of five databases was conducted. The inclusion criteria were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of exercise interventions lasting ≥ 4 weeks in patients with CRC. Robust Variance Estimation (RVE) was used to synthesize the overall effects of exercise interventions...

item.title: Psychosocial pathways linking PTSD and DSO symptoms to somatic symptoms among female North Korean defectors
item.description: Background: North Korean defectors (NKDs), approximately 72% of whom are female, are a trauma-exposed population in which somatic symptoms are common and culturally patterned. Previous research identified loneliness, perceived discrimination, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and disturbances in self-organization (DSO) symptoms as correlates of somatic symptoms. However, whether loneliness and perceived discrimination account for these relationships remains unclear.Objective: To examine...

item.title: Caregiver Experiences, Treatment Decision-Making, and Unmet Information Needs During Pediatric Growth Hormone Therapy: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey in Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: Caregivers of children receiving GH therapy reported substantial information needs and decision-making challenges despite generally positive treatment experiences. These caregiver-reported findings underscore the importance of improving communication, patient education, and shared decision-making to support informed treatment decisions in pediatric GH care.

item.title: Geographic disparities in fall-related emergency department visits among older adults in Korea: a nationwide time-series analysis and projection study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Korea faces a bifurcated geographic burden: metropolitan areas confront volume pressure, while non-metropolitan areas experience disproportionate severity. The future burden will be shaped by both unavoidable demographic ageing and potentially avertable increases in intrinsic fall risk. These findings have critical implications for rapidly ageing societies across East Asia facing comparable urban-rural disparities, necessitating regionally differentiated prevention and trauma care...

item.title: Three-Times-Daily 5% Diquafosol Versus Six-Times-Daily 3% Diquafosol for Dry Eye Disease: A Randomized, Double-Masked, Multicenter Phase 3 Noninferiority Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study found that 5% diquafosol demonstrated clinical efficacy and AE rates equivalent to those of 3% diquafosol, despite a halved dosing frequency. Therefore, 5% diquafosol may offer a more convenient treatment option for DED patients by reducing frequency.

item.title: Adjustment Disorders, Not Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: Mental Health Burden Among Conscription-Based Military Personnel in the Republic of Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Adjustment disorders-not PTSD-constitute the primary mental health burden in this conscription-based military system. These findings indicate that PTSD-centric frameworks derived from volunteer-force research may not apply to conscription-based systems, where transition-stress prevention may warrant greater priority than deployment-focused PTSD programs. The structural features of conscription systems-involuntary entry, hierarchical authority, and restricted autonomy-may shape a...

item.title: Long-Term Drop-Seizure Response Patterns to Cannabidiol According to Genetic Status in Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome
item.description: CONCLUSION: Long-term drop-seizure response to CBD in LGS was sustained but not stratified by genetic status, supporting a syndrome-level treatment approach irrespective of genetic findings.

item.title: Muscle, Nutritional, and Videofluoroscopic Factors Associated With 6-Month Oral Intake Recovery in Post-Stroke Dysphagia
item.description: CONCLUSION: Videofluoroscopic swallowing findings and indirect systemic vulnerability markers provided complementary information regarding 6-month oral intake recovery among stroke survivors after adjustment for stroke severity, cognition, aphasia, lesion characteristics, and major comorbidities.

item.title: Unit-Area Optimized Flexible Triboelectric Nanogenerators for High-Performance Human Motion Sensing With Deep Learning
item.description: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have garnered significant attention as self-powered energy harvesters and sensors, yet their performance critically depends on structural design and material engineering. In this work, we introduce a structured TENG designed with the concept of unit-area to maximize contact efficiency by minimizing mechanical interference between neighboring structures. Synergistically, barium titanate (BaTiO(3)) nanoparticles were incorporated into the elastomer matrix to...

item.title: Facile synthesis of large-Stokes-shift giant CdHgSe/CdHgSeS near-infrared quantum dots via chlorine-mediated Ostwald ripening
item.description: Giant core/shell quantum dots (GQDs) offer advantages for optoelectronics, including suppressed blinking and reduced Auger recombination, yet thick-shell growth often requires laborious successive ion layer adsorption and reaction (SILAR) cycles. Here we demonstrate a chlorine-mediated controlled Ostwald ripening strategy that transforms NIR-emitting CdHgSe/CdS core/shell seed QDs into giant CdHgSe/CdHgSeS core/gradient-shell QDs in a single post-synthetic step. Seed QDs are prepared by growing...

item.title: A Quantum-HPC Hybrid Workflow for Reaction-Center Electronic Dynamics: Application to a Cytochrome P450-Inspired Iron-Complex Model
item.description: We introduce population-transfer dynamics as a practical validation observable for active-state-derived reduced Hamiltonians in multistate reaction-center chemistry. In transition-metal systems, missing couplings or configurations can compromise the reliability of reduced active space models along a reaction coordinate, even when the overall spectrum is reproduced reasonably well. Using a cytochrome P450-inspired Fe-complex model, we construct a reaction-coordinate-dependent effective...

item.title: Global Epidemiology of Neonatal and Infantile-Onset Epilepsies and Epilepsy Syndromes (GENIE): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The findings underscore a significant global burden of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies, primarily driven by DEEs, specifically IESS. Given substantial between-study heterogeneity, the pooled estimates should be interpreted as broad indicators rather than precise, generalizable rates. Geographic disparities, with a lack of data from the African and Eastern Mediterranean Regions, underscore the need for population-based studies in underrepresented regions and...

item.title: Gastric cancer biomarker testing in Japan: a second nationwide survey of testing practices and associations with testing location
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although simultaneous four-biomarker testing is widely adopted in Japan, the use of in-house versus outsourced testing varies by biomarker and institution and is associated with differences in reported positivity rates. Our findings underscore the need for continued quality assurance and standardization to ensure reliable biomarker assessment and appropriate treatment selection.

item.title: Early changes in the urine-to-serum uric acid ratio are associated with subsequent eGFR slope during tolvaptan therapy in ADPKD
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The U/S UA ratio is a simple, clinically accessible index reflecting early physiological changes after tolvaptan initiation. Its association with subsequent eGFR decline appears partly influenced by changes in urine osmolality and requires prospective validation.

item.title: Real-world evidence supporting sustainable CAR-T-cell therapy-from access to long-term follow-up
item.description: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies and multiple myeloma. However, it involves multiple steps, from referral and eligibility assessment through leukapheresis, individualized manufacturing, bridging therapy, infusion, management of toxicities, and long-term follow-up, and requires multidisciplinary and interinstitutional health-care resources. Delay or failure at any step may compromise both access to CAR-T...

item.title: Emerging BCR::ABL1 inhibitors in chronic myeloid leukemia: current advances and future directions
item.description: Treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) has evolved beyond survival prolongation toward deeper molecular responses, long-term safety, and treatment-free remission. However, many patients still experience resistance, particularly with T315I and compound mutations, or intolerance to current tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), including ponatinib and the allosteric inhibitor asciminib, and cumulative toxicity during prolonged therapy remains a barrier to deep and durable responses. This review...

item.title: Decision vacuum and prepared delegation in cancer end-of-life decision-making: a scoping review
item.description: CONCLUSION: EOL support must transcend the rigid dichotomy between individual autonomy and delegation. Implementing the "prepared delegation" model through early intervention and multidisciplinary validation can eliminate the "decision vacuum," thereby preventing persistent decisional regret and protecting family economic and psychological well-being across the survivorship trajectory.

item.title: Municipal Progress in Community Building and Subsequent Individual Social Capital Among Older Adults in Japan: A Multilevel Longitudinal Study
item.description: Healthy ageing requires supportive environments beyond individual behaviors. Community building has gained policy attention, but evidence on how municipal progress in community building relates to individual social capital remains limited. We analyzed data from 91,891 older adults aged ≥ 65 years across 49 municipalities in Japan using the Japan Gerontological Evaluation Study (2019-2022). We examined whether municipal community-building progress in 2020 related to subsequent individual...

item.title: Salvage esophagectomy versus photodynamic therapy for localized residual or recurrent esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after definitive chemoradiotherapy or radiotherapy: a single-center comparative study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study does not establish equivalence or non-inferiority between PDT and salvage esophagectomy. PDT demonstrated a favorable safety profile and may offer an organ-preserving salvage treatment option for carefully selected patients with localized residual or recurrent ESCC after definitive CRT or RT, particularly those unsuitable for surgery because of advanced age, substantial comorbidities, or limited surgical tolerance.

item.title: Axially chiral P,olefin ligands for palladium-catalyzed asymmetric allylic amination with phthalimides
item.description: A Pd-catalyzed asymmetric allylic amination of allylic acetates with phthalimides has been developed using an axially chiral P,olefin ligand, affording allylic amines in excellent yields and enantioselectivities under mild conditions. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations identify a favored W-type pathway consistent with the observed absolute configuration. Structural comparisons and distortion-energy analysis suggest that the intermediate Pd-C bond asymmetry associated with the phosphine...

item.title: Geometric transition of latent dynamics in intermittent chaos: SVD-based effective dimension for detection and proactive control
item.description: This paper investigates the geometric detection of latent dynamic transitions (where the latent space is defined as a finite-dimensional state space reconstructed via a delay-embedding Hankel matrix) in mutually coupled phase-locked loops exhibiting on-off intermittent chaos. We propose a data-driven approach to identify the transition of the effective dimension in latent dynamics as a precursor to physical bursting events. By applying Singular Value Decomposition to a Hankel matrix constructed...

item.title: Optical detection of liquid-surface displacement associated with gas-bubble activity
item.description: Yeast produces carbon dioxide during fermentation, forming gas bubbles that immediately collapse and emit sound within the medium. This acoustic phenomenon has traditionally been monitored within the human hearing range to assess fermentation progress. Beyond the audible range, however, the bubbles also produce ultrasonic acoustic emissions, a fact that has been confirmed using hydrophones. I hypothesize that this information can be extracted by measuring vibrational motion at the liquid surface...

item.title: Changes in Health Literacy and Subsequent Presenteeism Among Workers: A Repeated-Measures Longitudinal Database Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: More positive HL changes were associated with modestly more favorable presenteeism outcomes. Direction-based associations were clear for decreases but not increases; larger increases showed favorable exploratory associations. Intervention effects require further study.

item.title: Boron trifluoride-catalyzed Diels-Alder reaction of α,β-unsaturated iminoindoles for the construction of 2-imino-3-spiroindoles
item.description: Despite the relevance of 2-imino-3-spiroindoles, particularly in medicinal chemistry, their synthesis still relies on highly reactive coupling partners. Herein, a novel approach to 2-imino-3-spiroindoles, involving the BF(3)-catalyzed Diels-Alder reaction of α,β-unsaturated iminoindoles with substituted dienes, is presented. The synthetic utility of this approach is demonstrated through the divergent derivatization of the resulting 2-imino-3-spiroindoles to produce various 3-spiroindole...

item.title: Multi-B-Site Cation Engineering in Stable Thiocyanate-Templated Layered Double-Perovskite Halides
item.description: Hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite halides offer a versatile structural platform owing to their flexible bonding nature. Beyond organic-cation engineering, halide-site engineering using molecular anions has recently emerged as an effective approach to alter the perovskite bonding network; however, accessible compositional and structural diversity remains limited. Here, we report, for the first time, hybrid layered Ag-Bi double perovskites, MA4AgBiX4(SCN)4 (X = Br, I), in which incorporation of...

item.title: Numerical investigation of the validity of Janak path integral and Slater-Janak theorem
item.description: Janak's theorem states that the derivative of the total energy with respect to an orbital occupation number equals the corresponding orbital energy. Integration of the Janak relation is referred to as the Janak path integral, and it connects the total energies of the N- and N-1- electron systems, yielding the ΔSCF ionization energy. We numerically assess the validity of the Janak path integral for ionization processes using both Hartree-Fock (HF) and Kohn-Sham (KS) methods. Although convergence...

item.title: A Large Multicenter Cohort of Ataxia-Telangiectasia: Clinical, Immunologic, Genetic, and Survival Outcomes
item.description: CONCLUSION: This large national cohort provides a comprehensive characterization of the clinical, immunologic, and genetic landscape of AT and its determinants of outcome, thereby improving diagnostic recognition, risk stratification, and patient management.

item.title: Peroneus Tertius as a Target in Targeted Muscle Reinnervation for the Management of Neuropathic Pain in the Leg: A Cadaveric Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: The peroneus tertius has MEP at a consistent location and plane and may be considered an optimal target for targeted muscle reinnervation around the foot and ankle.

item.title: Drinking-Water 4,4'-Methylenedianiline Establishes a Longitudinally Tractable Mouse Model of Cholestatic Liver Injury
item.description: Longitudinal studies of liver injury require models that can be maintained with simple administration, low procedure-related stress, and acceptable survival. Drinking-water thioacetamide (TAA-DW) is useful for this purpose, but it mainly produces centrilobular hepatocellular injury. Few drinking-water models are available for cholestatic liver injury. Here, we tested whether 4,4'-methylenedianiline (MDA), a known bile-duct-damaging hepatotoxicant, can be used to build a practical drinking-water...

item.title: Association between medial meniscus extrusion and joint effusion persistence at 1 month in knee osteoarthritis: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
item.description: [Purpose] Joint effusion is common in knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and contributes to functional limitations and disease progression. Persistence at 1 month is clinically relevant, as it may predispose patients to long-term effusion; however, the associated intra-articular lesions remain unclear. We aimed to identify intra-articular lesions associated with effusion persistence at 1 month using ultrasonography (US) for effusion quantification and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for lesion...

item.title: Relationship between the angle of trunk lateral tilt in the standing position and angle of trunk rotation during right and left hand-behind-back motion
item.description: [Purpose] This study examined the relationship between the angle of trunk lateral tilt and lateral trunk shift in the standing position and the angle of trunk rotation during right and left hand-behind-back motion. [Participants and Methods] We included twenty healthy, right-handed men. Hand-behind-back motion in the standing position was recorded using a three-dimensional motion-capture system. Correlations between the angle of trunk lateral tilt and lateral trunk shift in standing position and...

item.title: Recurrent Facial Paralysis in a 3-Month-Old Infant Associated With Acute Otitis Media: A Case Report
item.description: Acute otitis media (AOM) is a common pediatric condition, with facial nerve paralysis (FNP) as a rare complication. It occurs in approximately 0.004%-0.005% of cases. This report presents a unique case of a female infant with recurrent FNP related to AOM who experienced four episodes within the first 3 months of life. The patient was referred to our department at the 34th day of life with facial paralysis linked to left AOM. Treatment with intravenous antibiotics and systemic steroids initially...

item.title: The impact of preoperative nutritional status on recovery of physical function after lung resection for non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: [Purpose] This study examined the association between the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, an indicator for preoperative nutritional status, and postoperative recovery of physical function after lung resection in participants with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). [Participants and Methods] This study included 82 participants with NSCLC. Participants were classified into a normal group (0-1 point) and a light malnutrition group (2-4 points) based on their CONUT scores. The primary...

item.title: Baseline depressive-symptom severity and divergent psychological trajectories during GIP and/or GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy: a prospective ecological momentary assessment study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, baseline depressive-symptom severity was associated with divergent depressive-symptom trajectories during incretin receptor agonist therapy, whereas reductions in body weight and binge-eating tendency appeared independent of baseline mood.

item.title: Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was associated with a greater reduction in the FIB-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment. This finding should be interpreted as an exploratory association between a cell-specific transcriptomic feature and changes in a fibrosis-related index, rather than as evidence of functional SGLT2 signaling in monocytes or histological fibrosis regression.

item.title: Baseline monocyte GIP receptor mRNA expression is associated with reductions in body weight and FIB-4 index after switching to tirzepatide in patients with type 2 diabetes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Baseline monocyte GIPR mRNA expression was associated with body-weight and FIB-4 index reductions after switching to tirzepatide. It may represent an exploratory marker of clinical changes, but treatment specificity, causal GIPR-dependent mechanisms, and structural liver fibrosis regression were not established.

item.title: Student Characteristics Related to the Usability and Tolerability of a Metaverse-Based Anatomy Education System: A Cross-Sectional Study of 64 Medical Students
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Metaverse-based anatomy education could be considered broadly acceptable usability across diverse learners; however, tolerability varied according to student characteristics. Tailored support and careful implementation may be necessary to enhance safety and optimize learning experiences.

item.title: Analog Spin-Orbit Torque Switching in Vertically Graded Pt/Co-Re Heterostructures for Neuromorphic Computing
item.description: Achieving gradual, analog magnetization switching in spin-orbit torque (SOT) devices is essential for neuromorphic computing. In perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA)-based SOT devices, gradual switching can arise from domain nucleation, domain-wall propagation, and pinning, and controlling it through materials design remains a key goal. This study demonstrates that a vertically graded cobalt (Co)-rhenium (Re) alloy region, formed through a simple Co/Re multilayer design, enables analog SOT...

item.title: Plate or Screw Fixation in Proximal Phalangeal Fractures: An Interim Analysis of the POSI-P1 Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This interim analysis finds no difference in total active motion or patient- and clinician-reported outcome measures between the 3 interventions. Both dorsal plating and lateral plating require more surgical time to perform the intervention. Dorsal plating is significantly more likely to result in a major complication.

item.title: Diagnosing Rare Genetic Diseases From Facial Images Using Visual Prompting With Multimodal Large Language Models: Diagnostic Accuracy Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Under the evaluated experimental settings, the 3 MLLMs showed limited ability to diagnose rare genetic diseases from facial images, particularly diseases in GMDB-Rare. Visual prompting and image-to-phenotype diagnosis produced benefits in specific models and subgroups. The prediction-overlap, mismatched-image, and disease-composition analyses indicate that model outputs were only weakly constrained by patient-specific facial information. Further studies should evaluate physician...

item.title: Use of Large Language Models for Automated Short-Answer Question Grading in Second-Cycle Medical Education: Performance and Consistency Evaluation Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Advanced LLMs, particularly Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3, demonstrated near-human-level grading performance, supporting their potential use as assistive tools in SAQ grading. However, performance varied by model, and agreement alone does not ensure educational validity. Until broader multicenter validation is conducted across diverse domains, stakes, and question formats-along with safeguards for bias, privacy, and model drift-LLMs should augment rather than replace human faculty...

item.title: Consensus on Core Competencies of Undergraduate Life Sciences Students for Entry-Level Participation in Clinical Trials: RAND-Modified Delphi Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This consensus defines the core competencies required of undergraduate life sciences students for entry-level participation in clinical trial research. It also provides a framework for designing training strategies in both undergraduate and graduate programs of study.

item.title: Health Literacy in the Age of Digitalization in Switzerland: Cross-Sectional Representative Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study offers first insights into the DHL of the population in Switzerland and indicates that almost three-quarters (72.2%) of the population have low DHL. These results are in line with those of other European countries and clearly show the urgency of measures to improve DHL, especially among vulnerable population groups.

item.title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Spontaneous Affective Facial Responses for Cognitive Status Assessment in Older Adults: Exploratory Feasibility Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: AI-assisted analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses revealed differences in expression congruency and onset latency across cognitive performance levels. These preliminary findings suggest that AI-derived facial behavioral metrics may serve as noninvasive adjunctive features for observational cognitive assessment. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the exploratory design, modest sample size, and absence of internal or external validation.

item.title: Digital Resilience-Based Course-Game Sequential Intervention for Social Participation in Stroke Survivors: Development and Usability Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study systematically developed a theory-driven, digital course-game sequential intervention that is innovative in targeting psychological resilience as a core mechanism for social participation, distinguishing it from conventional function-focused or generic resilience approaches. By integrating systematic course learning with contextualized gamified practice, it offers a scalable, low-burden tool that addresses key gaps in stroke rehabilitation. These findings support...

item.title: A Randomized Factorial Trial of Varenicline, Nicotine Lozenges, and Smartphone Medication Adherence Reminders for Smoking Cessation: Protocol for the COMBO II Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: If effective, VAR+NRT would offer a new evidence-based cessation treatment option. If the smartphone adherence intervention improves medication adherence and cessation, it could be adapted for other pharmacotherapies and widely implemented. Ultimately, this research aims to enhance cessation efforts and reduce cancer risk among adults who smoke.

item.title: In Vivo Detection of Ampullary T2 Hypointensity as a Marker of Vestibular Atelectasis
item.description: CONCLUSION: A T2 hypointense signal within the ampullae and utricle was observed exclusively in patients with radiological vestibular atelectasis in this cohort. Its anatomical distribution is compatible with the basophilic deposits described in histopathological series, although this correspondence remains hypothetical in the absence of tissue analysis. This MRI sign may raise suspicion of VA when delayed postcontrast 3D-FLAIR imaging is unavailable or contraindicated, rather than replace it.

item.title: Germline Genetic Variants and Epilepsy Surgery Response: Individual Participant Pooled Analysis of 272 Patients
item.description: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Genetic testing is increasingly used in presurgical evaluation, but the yield of resection and ablation across germline genetic epilepsies remains uncertain.

item.title: Developing a core outcome set for Meniere's disease trials, the COSMED study: results from two separate, two-round Delphi surveys on outcome domains and outcomes

item.title: Noninvasive Insights: Magnetic Resonance Elastography and Ultrasound Liver Elastography for the Assessment of Liver Fibrosis in Fontan-Associated Liver Disease: A Comparative Study with Histology
item.description: The diagnostic performance of ultrasound (U/S) elastography and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) of liver relative to histological assessment in Fontan patients remains uncertain. This study sought to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and agreement of MRE and U/S elastography compared with histological congestive hepatic fibrosis score (CHFS) staging. item.title: Phage N4 uses a SAR endolysin-holin system for host cell lysis
item.description: Bacteriophages (phages) cause active host cell lysis to terminate their infection and release progeny into the environment. However, some phages have systems to delay their lysis, and thereby increase progeny yield, in specific conditions: a phenomenon called lysis inhibition (LIN). Two dissimilar phages of Escherichia coli are known to exhibit LIN: T4 and N4. In T4, a multi-protein mechanism stalls lysis and maintains the LIN state in response to superinfection in a high phage population...

item.title: From theory to practice: a "Clarify-Bridge-Practice" seminar model for graduate medical trainees entering cardiovascular research
item.description: Graduate students in clinical medicine often possess advanced theoretical knowledge but struggle to translate it into testable hypotheses and feasible experimental designs-a "knowing-doing" gap particularly pronounced in cardiovascular physiology. To address this, we developed and evaluated a "Clarify-Bridge-Practice" (CBP) seminar model in a cardiovascular course with 87 graduate students across three cohorts (2023-2025). item.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Endoureterotomy in Children with Primary Obstructive Megaureter: A Single-Center Experience
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study suggests that endoureterotomy, as a minimally invasive surgical approach, provides favorable long-term ultrasonographic and scintigraphic outcomes with a high success rate in selected children with POM.

item.title: Functional export of NDM-7 to outer membrane vesicles in Klebsiella pneumoniae compromises imipenem and cefiderocol activity
item.description: The carbapenemases Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC) and New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM) are the most widespread determinants of carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae. Whereas KPC is a soluble periplasmic serine-β-lactamase, NDM is a membrane-anchored metallo-β-lactamase (MBL), a feature that promotes its incorporation into outer membrane vesicles (OMVs).
